rdfs:label: DIDDocument
rdfs:comment: The descriptor for a Decentralized Identifier — carries the DID's verification keys, service endpoints, and controller relationships.
notes: What you get when you resolve a DID. Contains everything needed to verify proofs signed by that DID and discover services it offers. The DID itself is the document's `@id`. Most decentralised-identity flows start by resolving a DID to its Document and pulling a `verificationMethod` out. Upstream the class is `did:DIDSubject` (rdfs:label "DID Document" in https://www.w3.org/ns/did) — there is no `did:DIDDocument`. DID Core documents usually omit `@type`, so typing a document with this class is optional; it is mostly useful for typing the subject explicitly in RDF. In a DID document, `verificationMethod` usually holds embedded key objects rather than bare references.

history.note: Remapped owl:sameAs from non-existent did:DIDDocument to did:DIDSubject (labelled 'DID Document' upstream); noted @type is optional; example embeds a verification method object.
